Class State

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Numbered
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.State
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<State>
public class State extends Numbered implements Comparable<State>
A state defines a value for each fluent and a numeric utility value for a story and each character in a story graph.

Every node has a state. States do not model character beliefs. State objects are distinct from node objects because nodes which are not the same (due to having different character beliefs) may still have the same values for each fluent and character, allowing state object to be reused to save memory.

New states are usually not created directly but as a result of adding new nodes to the story graph.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware

    • getUtility

      public double getUtility(Character character)
      Returns the utility for the given character, which is how desirable that character considers this state to be. If the character given is null, this method returns the author's utility. If the character has no utility value in this state, perhaps because it was added to the story graph after this state was created, this method returns Double.NaN.
      Parameters:
      character - the character whose utility is desired
      Returns:
      the character's utility

    • prune

      protected void prune(Predicate<Object> predicate)
      Removes any pruned elements from this element, and if this element itself should be pruned its ID number will be set to Settings.PRUNED.

      If any fluent has a nominal value whose ID number has been set to Settings.PRUNED those values will be replaced with null.

      Overrides:
      prune in class Numbered
      Parameters:
      predicate - a predicate which returns true for any story graph element that should be removed
